strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the reopened semantic protocol/event contract blocker with a Runtime-owned generated contract, golden Rust-to-VSIX fixture tests, and guard-enforced drift detection so external controllers can depend on stable request/result semantics.
Keeps protocol semantics, unknown-field rejection, enum handling, and durable event migration coupling inside Runtime/protocol/store authority rather than CLI, VSIX, prose, or model output.
Preserves controlled JSON-RPC and MCP tool execution boundaries by making public Runtime params fail closed on unknown fields while leaving tool execution authority in Rust Runtime.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by turning the RRP-5.2 full method inventory into recursive Rust-derived wire schemas and concrete ledger payload-shape fingerprints.
answers.new_capability: The checked-in Runtime semantic protocol contract now includes recursive JSON Schema documents for all method param/result types, method refs and recursive fingerprints, and payload-envelope fingerprints derived from actual payload structure rather than event-kind version labels alone.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-5.2 proved all 51 method names and top-level fields, but nested object/enum/array shapes and concrete ledger payload fields could still drift without a machine-detected recursive schema or payload-shape fingerprint change.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless controller could receive a nested result or ledger payload whose internal shape changed while the top-level method contract and event-kind version label stayed unchanged.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-5.3 corrective for recursive nested wire schemas and concrete ledger payload shape fingerprints; it does not repeat RRP-5.2 method coverage, RRP-7.1 terminal/deadline work, RRP-4.1 durable migration recovery, or CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-5.3 adds no JSON-RPC method and instead deepens generated schema evidence for the existing public Runtime methods.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new JSON artifact is release evidence generated by Rust protocol code, not a runtime diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, dashboard, or user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Task ledger events with payloads now compute payload_envelope.shape_fingerprint from the structural shape of the actual payload value, including field names, primitive kinds, arrays, nested objects, and nulls.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation gets machine-checkable recursive request/result compatibility and payload shape drift evidence across the explicit Runtime API set.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the reopened recursive protocol/ledger payload schema gap while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until platform-deadline-durability-hardening, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

exit_criteria: docs/architecture/runtime-semantic-protocol-contract.json is generated by brownie-protocol and covers every explicit Runtime method in the canonical map.
The generated artifact includes recursive type_schemas with $defs for nested structs/enums and every method records request/result schema refs plus recursive schema fingerprints.

Rust tests prove artifact freshness, canonical-map method set equality, all-public-params unknown-field policy evidence, recursive nested schema refs, enum values, and fixture serialization semantics.

VSIX tests consume the generated artifact and prove canonical method coverage, nested type_schemas, validators reject unknown fields, payload envelope fixture evidence, and task.start projection matches Rust wire params.

guard:protocol-event-canonization fails when explicit method contracts, recursive type schemas, all-public-param deny-unknown evidence, VSIX test evidence, or concrete ledger payload shape migration coupling is removed.
recursive protocol/ledger payload schema coverage is closed while Runtime Release Ready remains false and platform-deadline-durability-hardening plus runtime-release-guard-ci remain open.

accepted_capability: Rust protocol crate owns and generates the full explicit Runtime semantic protocol contract artifact.
The semantic contract includes recursive JSON Schema for all method param/result types, including nested structs/enums through $defs.
VSIX validates generated golden fixtures, canonical method coverage, nested schema refs, and projection semantics against that artifact.
All public Runtime params covered by RRP-5.2/RRP-5.3 reject unknown fields in Rust and are recorded in generated semantic evidence.
Durable ledger payload shape changes are coupled to explicit store schema migration policy through payload envelopes whose fingerprints include concrete payload structure.
behavior_evidence: Rust semantic_contract tests cover generator freshness, canonical method-set equality, recursive nested schema refs, public-param unknown-field policy, and serde semantics.
brownie-store tests prove payload field and nested-shape changes alter ledger payload shape fingerprints.
VSIX semanticProtocolContract tests cover validators, request projection, canonical coverage, nested type_schemas, and payload envelope fixture evidence.
guard:protocol-event-canonization and its tests enforce RRP-5.3 evidence through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/protocol/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
